definition_zh: v. 阐明；解释；使清楚；阐释
definition_en: to make something clear by explaining it
core_image: 一束手电光扫过写满术语的黑板，每照到一行，旁边就浮出一句白话解释
scene: 研讨室里投影上是一页密密麻麻的公式，主讲人拿起激光笔逐行点过去，把每个符号换成一句白话。The diagram helped to elucidate the mechanism of the reaction.
sceneCN: 这里 elucidate 指「阐明」（第 1 个义项：把难懂的内容讲清楚）；句意是那张示意图帮助阐明了反应机理。

pos.zh: 阐明；解释；使清楚

senses.title: To make clear
senses.definition: to explain something so that it becomes clear
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把某事讲明白，使人听懂
senses.example: The teacher elucidated the rule with a single drawing.
senses.exampleCN: 老师用一张图就把这条规则阐明了。
senses.why: A torch beam crossing a blackboard until every symbol has a plain sentence beside it
senses.whyCN: 一束手电光扫过黑板，直到每个符号旁边都有一句白话

senses.title: To shed light on a text
senses.definition: to explain the meaning of a difficult passage
senses.definitionCN: （动词）解释一段难懂文字的意思
senses.example: A footnote elucidates the archaic word in the poem.
senses.exampleCN: 一条脚注阐释了诗中那个古词。
senses.why: A small lamp held over a faded page so the old letters can be read
senses.whyCN: 一盏小灯举在褪色书页上方，好让那些旧字母能被读出来

senses.title: To clarify by detail
senses.definition: to make an idea plain by adding examples or detail
senses.definitionCN: （动词）通过补充例子或细节使想法清楚
senses.example: She elucidated her proposal with three case studies.
senses.exampleCN: 她用三个案例把自己的提案说明白了。
senses.why: A sketch map with three numbered stops added one at a time
senses.whyCN: 一张草图地图上逐个添上三个编号站点

intro.en: Elucidate comes from Latin e- meaning out and lucidus meaning bright, from lux meaning light; to elucidate is to bring a thing out into the light.
intro.cn: elucidate 来自拉丁语 e-（向外）与 lucidus（明亮的），后者源自 lux（光）；elucidate 就是把事物带到光下。

items.en: Lux means light, the source of lucidus and of many English words about brightness.
items.cn: lux 意为光，是 lucidus 的来源，也是英语中许多与光亮有关词语的源头。

items.en: Lucidus means bright or clear, and gives English lucid.
items.cn: lucidus 意为明亮或清楚，给出英语 lucid。

items.en: Late Latin elucidare means to make clear, built from e- plus lucidus.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 elucidare 意为使清楚，由 e- 加 lucidus 构成。

items.en: English takes elucidate in the 1560s for explaining a difficult text.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪 60 年代吸收 elucidate，用于解释难懂的文本。

items.en: The noun elucidation becomes common in scholarly commentary.
items.cn: 名词 elucidation 在学术注释中变得常见。

items.en: Researchers elucidate mechanisms and structures, extending the word to science.
items.cn: 研究者阐明机理与结构，把这个词扩展到科学领域。

note.en: Elucidate, illuminate and lucid all share the Latin root for light; clarify and explain are the everyday equivalents.
note.cn: elucidate、illuminate 与 lucid 共享拉丁语「光」的词根；clarify 与 explain 是日常对应词。

dict_mnemonic.text: elucidate ＝ e-（向外）＋ lucid（清楚的，拉丁 lucidus「明亮」，源自 lux「光」）＋ -ate（动词后缀）＝「把东西搬到光下」。名词 elucidation，同根形容词 lucid 清楚的、名词 lucidity 清晰、translucent 半透明的、illuminate 照亮。及物动词，宾语是难懂的内容：elucidate a point 阐明论点、elucidate the mechanism 阐明机理、elucidate a text 阐释文本。常用于学术与科技写作，语气比 explain 正式。近义 clarify 侧重消除混乱，explicate 侧重逐层展开文本，interpret 侧重给出意义；elucidate 强调用光照亮式的讲明白。

root: 拉丁语 e-（向外）＋ lucidus（明亮的，源自 lux「光」）→ elucidare（使清楚）→ elucidate（阐明）

definition_zh: adj. 难捉摸的；难懂的；难找到的；难以实现的
definition_en: difficult to catch, find, understand or achieve
core_image: 伸手去拢雾里的一只蝴蝶，网口刚合上，它已经从网眼边滑走
scene: 雾里一只蝴蝶停在叶尖，男孩把网兜慢慢合拢，它却从网眼边滑走了。An elusive butterfly slipped out of the closing net.
sceneCN: 这里 elusive 指「难捕捉的」（第 1 个义项：难以抓住或找到）；句意是一只难捕捉的蝴蝶从正在合拢的网里滑走了。

pos.zh: 难捉摸的；难懂的；难找到的

senses.title: Hard to catch
senses.definition: difficult to catch, find or reach
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）难以抓住、找到或够到
senses.example: The leopard proved elusive, and the camera traps recorded only leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 那只豹子始终难以捕捉，红外相机只拍到了树叶。
senses.why: A butterfly leaving the net at the exact moment the rim closes
senses.whyCN: 网口合拢的那一刻蝴蝶离开网兜

senses.title: Hard to define
senses.definition: difficult to describe or understand precisely
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）难以准确描述或理解
senses.example: Happiness is an elusive concept that no survey can pin down.
senses.exampleCN: 幸福是个难以界定的概念，任何问卷都抓不住它。
senses.why: Sugar dissolving in a closed hand before the fingers can hold it
senses.whyCN: 糖在合拢的手心里化掉，手指还来不及握住

senses.title: Hard to recall or attain
senses.definition: difficult to remember or to achieve
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）难以回想起来或难以达成
senses.example: The title of the song remained elusive long after the melody came back.
senses.exampleCN: 旋律早就想起来了，歌名却迟迟记不起。
senses.why: A name standing on the tip of the tongue and then stepping back
senses.whyCN: 名字停在舌尖上，随后又退了回去

intro.en: Elusive comes from Latin e- meaning out and ludere meaning to play; eludere is to escape by slipping away, like a fish that leaves the hands.
intro.cn: elusive 来自拉丁语 e-（向外）与 ludere（玩耍）；eludere 意为靠滑脱逃身，像一条从手中溜走的鱼。

items.en: Ludere means to play, and gives English illusion and allusion.
items.cn: ludere 意为玩耍，给出英语 illusion 与 allusion。

items.en: Eludere means to escape or to mock, built from e- plus ludere.
items.cn: eludere 意为逃脱或戏弄，由 e- 加 ludere 构成。

items.en: Elusus is the past participle, meaning slipped away or escaped.
items.cn: elusus 是过去分词，意为溜走或逃脱。

items.en: English forms elusive from elusus on the pattern of abusive and delusive.
items.cn: 英语按 abusive 与 delusive 的构词模式，由 elusus 造出 elusive。

items.en: The noun elusiveness appears in criticism and in philosophy.
items.cn: 名词 elusiveness 出现在批评与哲学文字中。

items.en: Elusive spreads to targets, memories and results that stay out of reach.
items.cn: elusive 扩展到始终够不着的目标、记忆与结果。

note.en: Elusive, elude and illusion share the Latin root ludere, to play; evasive and intangible are the nearest everyday synonyms.
note.cn: elusive、elude 与 illusion 共享拉丁词根 ludere（玩耍）；evasive 与 intangible 是最接近的日常同义词。

dict_mnemonic.text: elusive ＝ e-（向外）＋ lus（玩耍，拉丁 ludere，过去分词 elusus「溜走」）＋ -ive（形容词后缀）＝「像玩一样溜出去的」。动词 elude 逃避、使困惑，副词 elusively，名词 elusiveness；同根 illusion 幻觉、allusion 典故、delude 欺骗。三类用法：抓不住 an elusive butterfly 难捕捉的蝴蝶、an elusive criminal 在逃的罪犯；说不清 an elusive concept 难以界定的概念、an elusive meaning 捉摸不定的含义；够不着 an elusive goal 难以实现的目标、elusive memory 想不起的记忆。常与 remain、prove 连用：remain elusive 仍然难以捉摸。比较级用 more elusive，没有 elusiver。近义 evasive 侧重故意回避，intangible 侧重无形，slippery 侧重滑脱；elusive 强调你越追它越溜。注意与 allusive（用典的）只差一个字母。

root: 拉丁语 e-（向外）＋ ludere（玩耍）→ eludere（逃脱）→ elusus（溜走的）→ elusive（难捉摸的）

definition_zh: v. 使消瘦；使憔悴；使衰弱
definition_en: to make a person or animal extremely thin and weak
core_image: 饥荒照片里一个人坐着，锁骨和肋骨一根根凸起，外套空荡荡地挂在肩上
scene: 救济站门口排着长队，一个男人坐下时外套从肩上滑下去，锁骨和肋骨一根根凸起。The photograph showed a man emaciated by months of hunger.
sceneCN: 这里 emaciate 指「使消瘦」（第 1 个义项：因缺食而极度消瘦，此处用被动）；句意是照片里的男人被数月的饥饿拖得形销骨立。

pos.zh: 使消瘦；使憔悴；使衰弱

senses.title: To make thin
senses.definition: to make a person or animal extremely thin through lack of food
senses.definitionCN: （动词）因缺食而使人或动物极度消瘦
senses.example: Months of drought emaciated the herd before the rains came.
senses.exampleCN: 数月的干旱让畜群在雨季来临前瘦得脱了形。
senses.why: A coat slipping off a shoulder because the body inside has shrunk
senses.whyCN: 外套从肩上滑落，因为里面的身体缩掉了

senses.title: To waste through illness
senses.definition: to weaken and thin the body through illness or hardship
senses.definitionCN: （动词）因疾病或苦难而使身体衰弱消瘦
senses.example: The fever emaciated him faster than the doctors expected.
senses.exampleCN: 那场热病让他消瘦得比医生预料的更快。
senses.why: Ribs standing out like the bars of an empty cage
senses.whyCN: 肋骨根根凸起，像空笼子的栅栏

senses.title: To become wasted
senses.definition: to grow thin and weak, usually in the passive voice
senses.definitionCN: （动词）变得消瘦虚弱，通常用于被动语态
senses.example: The rescued dog was emaciated but still able to stand.
senses.exampleCN: 获救的狗已经瘦得脱形，但仍能站起来。
senses.why: A candle burned down to a thin thread of wax
senses.whyCN: 蜡烛烧到只剩细细一条蜡

intro.en: Emaciate comes from Latin e- meaning out and macies meaning leanness, from macer meaning thin; to emaciate is to let the flesh waste away.
intro.cn: emaciate 来自拉丁语 e-（向外）与 macies（瘦削），后者源自 macer（瘦的）；emaciate 就是让血肉耗损下去。

items.en: Macer means thin or lean, and gives English meagre.
items.cn: macer 意为瘦或贫瘦，给出英语 meagre。

items.en: Macies means leanness or wasting, the noun behind emaciate.
items.cn: macies 意为瘦削或耗损，是 emaciate 背后的名词。

items.en: Emaciare means to make lean, built from e- plus macies.
items.cn: emaciare 意为使瘦，由 e- 加 macies 构成。

items.en: Emaciatus is the past participle, meaning wasted away.
items.cn: emaciatus 是过去分词，意为耗损殆尽。

items.en: English takes emaciate in the 1610s as a medical and formal verb.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪 10 年代吸收 emaciate，作为医学与正式用语的动词。

items.en: Emaciation becomes the standard term in reports on famine and disease.
items.cn: emaciation 成为饥荒与疾病报告中的标准用词。

note.en: Emaciate, macerate and meagre share the Latin root macer, thin; the nearest verbal synonyms are waste, starve and wither.
note.cn: emaciate、macerate 与 meagre 共享拉丁词根 macer（瘦）；最接近的动词同义词是 waste、starve 与 wither。

dict_mnemonic.text: emaciate ＝ e-（向外）＋ maci（瘦，拉丁 macies「瘦削」，源自 macer「瘦的」）＋ -ate（动词后缀）＝「把血肉耗出去」。名词 emaciation 消瘦、憔悴；同根 macerate 浸软、使消瘦，maceration 浸软，meagre 贫乏的、瘦的。及物动词，主语是饥饿、疾病、干旱等消耗性因素：emaciate the body 使身体消瘦。现代英语更常用被动或过去分词作形容词：emaciated by hunger 饿得形销骨立、an emaciated prisoner 消瘦的囚犯、severely emaciated 极度消瘦的。医学与新闻语体常见，日常口语多说 very thin 或 starved。近义 waste 强调耗损，starve 强调断食，wither 强调枯萎；emaciate 强调瘦到骨头凸起的程度。注意与 emanate（散发）拼写相近但词根不同。

root: 拉丁语 e-（向外）＋ macies（瘦削，源自 macer「瘦的」）→ emaciare（使瘦）→ emaciatus → emaciate（使消瘦）

sensesIntro.en: Three pictures of a body wasting away: a coat slipping off a shoulder, ribs like cage bars and a candle burned down to a thread.
sensesIntro.cn: 身体耗损的三幅画面：从肩上滑落的外套、像笼子栅栏的肋骨，以及烧到只剩细线的蜡烛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coat slipping off a shoulder because the body inside has shrunk
core.cn: 核心意象：外套从肩上滑落，因为里面的身体缩掉了

branches.en: Hunger takes the flesh away.
branches.cn: 饥饿把血肉带走。

branches.en: Illness burns the body down.
branches.cn: 疾病把身体烧耗下去。

branches.en: The body is left thin and weak.
branches.cn: 身体只剩消瘦虚弱。

branches.en: Both empty a body from outside.
branches.cn: 两者都从外部掏空身体。

branches.en: Both end in the same wasted state.
branches.cn: 两者都终于同一种耗损状态。

intro.en: Emaciate is e- plus mac- plus -ate; -ation gives emaciation, and the same root gives macerate and meagre.
intro.cn: emaciate 由 e- 加 mac- 加 -ate 组成；-ation 给出 emaciation，同一词根给出 macerate 与 meagre。

latinIntro.en: Latin macer means thin, macies leanness and macerare to soak soft; these give emaciate, meagre and macerate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 macer 意为瘦，macies 意为瘦削，macerare 意为浸软；这些给出 emaciate、meagre 与 macerate。

definition_zh: 电子邮件；电子邮件系统；发电子邮件
definition_en: a message sent electronically over a network; the email system; to send such a message
core_image: 一封信化作光点，沿着看不见的线飞进对方的屏幕
scene: 地铁进站前，她低头用手机把收件箱刷了一遍，未读的小红点一个个消失。She checked her email before the train arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 email 是「电子邮件」（第 1 个义项：通过网络发送的电子信件）；句意是列车到站前她查看了邮件。

pos.zh: 电子邮件；电子邮件系统
发电子邮件

derivatives.zh: 发邮件的人或邮件程序

senses.title: A message sent over a network
senses.definition: a written message sent from one computer or phone to another through the internet
senses.definitionCN: 通过互联网从一台电脑或手机发送到另一台的书面信息
senses.example: She checked her email before the train arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 列车到站前她查看了邮件。
senses.why: The word joins electronic and mail, so an old paper letter keeps its name while its body turns into data travelling through wires.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 electronic 与 mail 合成，纸信的名字被保留下来，但信的内容变成了沿线路传输的数据。

senses.title: The email system
senses.definition: the whole system of accounts, servers and software used to send such messages
senses.definitionCN: 用来发送这类信息的账号、服务器与软件构成的整套系统
senses.example: The company moved all its email to the cloud.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把所有邮件系统都迁移到了云端。
senses.why: A single message and the network that carries it share one name, so email also means the postal system of the internet.
senses.whyCN: 单封邮件与承载它的网络共用一个名字，所以 email 也指互联网上的那套邮政系统。

senses.title: To send an email
senses.definition: to send a message to someone using email
senses.definitionCN: 用电子邮件给某人发送信息
senses.example: Please email me the draft by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 请在周五前把草稿发邮件给我。
senses.why: Any mail noun in English can turn into a verb meaning to send it, so email follows mail and letter into action.
senses.whyCN: 英语里凡是「邮件」类名词都能转成表示「寄送」的动词，email 于是跟着 mail 一起从物品变成了动作。

intro.en: Email is a twentieth-century compound of electronic and mail, with mail itself coming from an old word for a bag.
intro.cn: email 是二十世纪由 electronic 与 mail 合成的词，而 mail 本身来自一个表示「袋子」的古老词。

items.en: Male meant a bag or bundle, especially a traveller's pack.
items.cn: 古法语 male 指袋子或包裹，尤指旅人的行囊。

items.en: English mail first meant a bag of letters, then the letters themselves.
items.cn: 中古英语 mail 先指一袋信件，后来指信件本身。

items.en: The postal sense became standard in Britain and America.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，邮政义在英美成为标准用法。

items.en: Computing coined electronic mail for messages passed between machines.
items.cn: 计算机领域造出 electronic mail，指机器之间传递的信息。

items.en: The clipped form email replaced the longer phrase and then became a verb.
items.cn: 缩略形式 email 取代了较长短语，随后又用作动词。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the mail family; the near-meaning group separates a message, a paper letter and the place where mail waits.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 mail 词族展开；近义组区分一条信息、一封纸质信与收件的地方。

entries.definition: Letters and parcels sent by post, or the system that carries them.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「邮件、邮政」，是本词的基础。

entries.definition: The older hyphenated spelling of the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的旧式连字符拼写。

entries.definition: A box where mail is delivered or stored.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，义为「信箱」，也可指电子邮箱。

entries.definition: A piece of information sent to someone, by any channel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「消息」，可经任何渠道传递。

entries.definition: A written message on paper, usually posted.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「信件」，通常写在纸上邮寄。

entries.definition: The folder where incoming email is collected.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「收件箱」，是邮件到达后聚集的地方。

normalIntro.en: These hooks read email as electronic mail, then follow the letter into a message, a system and a verb.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 email 读成「电子的邮件」，再让这封信变成消息、系统与动作。

normal.en: Electronic plus mail gives email.
normal.cn: electronic 加 mail 就是 email。

normal.en: Mail first meant a bag of letters.
normal.cn: mail 最早指装信的一只袋子。

normal.en: An email address is the electronic version of a house address.
normal.cn: email address 就是电子版的门牌地址。

normal.en: You can email a file or a person.
normal.cn: 你可以把文件或人「邮件」一下，也就是发信给对象。

normal.en: The inbox is the mailbox of the screen.
normal.cn: 收件箱就是屏幕里的信箱。

abstract.en: Picture a paper letter dissolving into sparks that fly along a wire.
abstract.cn: 想象一封纸信化成火花，沿着线路飞走。

abstract.en: A message and the system that carries it wear the same name.
abstract.cn: 一条消息与承载它的系统穿着同一个名字。

abstract.en: The word is a post office squeezed into a screen.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是一家被塞进屏幕的邮局。

examples.en: She checked her email before the train arrived.
examples.cn: 列车到站前她查看了邮件。

examples.en: The company moved all its email to the cloud.
examples.cn: 公司把所有邮件系统都迁移到了云端。

examples.en: Please email me the draft by Friday.
examples.cn: 请在周五前把草稿发邮件给我。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊妹儿」——网络上飞来的电子信件

root: 由 electronic（电子的）与 mail（邮件）缩合而成；mail 出自古法语 male（袋子），原指一袋信件。

sensesIntro.en: Email names one electronic letter, then the whole electronic postal system, and finally the act of sending.
sensesIntro.cn: email 先指一封电子信件，再指整套电子邮政系统，最后指发送这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a letter turning into sparks and flying through a wire.
core.cn: 核心意象：一封信化作火花，沿着线路飞向远方。

branches.en: THE LETTER: one message arriving in a screen.
branches.cn: 信件线：一条消息抵达屏幕。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: accounts, servers and software as one post office.
branches.cn: 系统线：账号、服务器与软件合成一家邮局。

branches.en: THE ACTION: to send such a message.
branches.cn: 动作线：发送这样一条消息。

branches.en: ITEM AND NETWORK: one letter and the network that carries it.
branches.cn: 单件与网络：一封信和承载它的网络。

branches.en: THING AND ACT: the object becomes the verb.
branches.cn: 物与动作：名词转成动词。

intro.en: Email is a clipped compound: e- stands for electronic and mail supplies the postal meaning.
intro.cn: email 是缩合复合词：e- 代表 electronic，mail 提供邮政含义。

latinIntro.en: The mail part is Germanic through French, and there is no single Latin etymon for the compound.
latinIntro.cn: mail 这一部分经法语来自日耳曼语，整个复合词没有单一的拉丁词源。

items.example: It stands for electronic in email.
items.exampleCN: 它在 email 中代表 electronic。

items.meaning: more than one, or he does

items.exampleCN: 它由 mail 与 box 合成。

definition_zh: n. 堤岸；路堤；防洪堤；筑堤
definition_en: a long raised bank of earth or stone built to carry a road or to hold back water
core_image: 一条高出稻田的土埂，两侧斜面压着石块，埂顶铺着铁轨，河水在埂脚外打着旋
scene: 洪水涨到离埂顶只剩一掌宽，巡堤人踩着湿草来回走，土埂另一侧就是熟睡的村子。The embankment held the river back from the sleeping village.
sceneCN: 这里 embankment 指「防洪堤」（第 2 个义项：挡住河水的土堤）；句意是堤岸把河水挡在熟睡的村庄之外。

pos.zh: 堤岸；路堤；筑堤

senses.title: A raised bank of earth
senses.definition: a long mound of earth or stone built to carry a road or railway
senses.definitionCN: （名词）为承载道路或铁路而垒起的长条土石堆
senses.example: The train ran along an embankment above the flooded fields.
senses.exampleCN: 火车沿着高出淹水田地的路堤行驶。
senses.why: A long earth ridge carrying a railway above wet fields
senses.whyCN: 一条长长的土埂把铁路托在湿田之上

senses.title: A wall against water
senses.definition: a bank built to keep a river or the sea from flooding land
senses.definitionCN: （名词）为挡住河水或海水淹没陆地而筑的堤
senses.example: The embankment held the river back from the sleeping village.
senses.exampleCN: 堤岸把河水挡在熟睡的村庄之外。
senses.why: A river pushing all night at the foot of a stone-faced bank
senses.whyCN: 河水整夜推着石面堤的堤脚

senses.title: The act of banking up
senses.definition: the work of building such a bank
senses.definitionCN: （名词）修筑这种堤岸的工程
senses.example: They built the embankment from three hundred carts of earth.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用三百车土筑起了这道堤。
senses.why: Cartloads of earth tipped and pressed into a rising ridge
senses.whyCN: 一车车土倒下、压实，垒成越来越高的土埂

intro.en: Embankment is em- plus bank plus -ment; bank comes from Old Norse banki, a ridge of earth, and -ment turns the verb into the thing built.
intro.cn: embankment 由 em- 加 bank 加 -ment 组成；bank 来自古诺斯语 banki（土埂），-ment 把动词变成造出来的东西。

items.en: Banki means a ridge of earth; Old English banca has the same sense, and both feed English bank.
items.cn: banki 意为土埂；古英语 banca 同义，两者共同汇入英语 bank。

items.en: Banke is used for the edge of a river and for a raised mound.
items.cn: banke 用来指河岸，也指隆起的土堆。

items.en: The verb embank appears, meaning to enclose or protect with a bank.
items.cn: 动词 embank 出现，意为用堤围住或保护。

items.en: Embankment is formed with -ment for the bank itself and the work of building it.
items.cn: embankment 加 -ment 构成，指堤本身，也指筑堤的工程。

items.en: Railway builders use embankment for the raised earth carrying the track.
items.cn: 铁路建设者用 embankment 指承载轨道的高起土方。

items.en: Embankment becomes a standard term in flood defence and river engineering.
items.cn: embankment 成为防洪与河流工程中的标准用词。

note.en: Embankment, embank and sandbank all build on bank, a ridge of earth; levee and dyke are the nearest synonyms.
note.cn: embankment、embank 与 sandbank 都建立在 bank（土埂）之上；levee 与 dyke 是最接近的同义词。

entries.definition: to enclose or protect with a bank
a ridge of sand in a river or the sea
a recess in a coastline or a bay
a raised bank along a river that stops flooding
a bank or wall built to keep out water
a raised pile of earth or stones

normalIntro.en: Picture a long earth ridge with a railway on top and a river pushing at its foot.
normalIntro.cn: 想象一条长长的土埂，顶上铺着铁轨，河水在埂脚推着。

normal.en: A ridge of earth carries the track above the wet fields.
normal.cn: 一条土埂把轨道托在湿田之上。

normal.en: The river pushes at the foot of the bank all night.
normal.cn: 河水整夜推着堤脚。

normal.en: A man walks the top with a lamp, reading the water line.
normal.cn: 一个人提着灯在埂顶走，读着水痕。

normal.en: Bank is a ridge, and the suffix is the thing that has been built.
normal.cn: 词根是土埂，后缀是造出来的东西。

normal.en: Stones are pressed into the slope so the earth cannot slide.
normal.cn: 石块被压进斜面，好让土滑不下来。

abstract.en: A long earth ridge carrying a railway above wet fields
abstract.cn: 一条长长的土埂把铁路托在湿田之上

abstract.en: A river pushing all night at the foot of a stone-faced bank
abstract.cn: 河水整夜推着石面堤的堤脚

abstract.en: Cartloads of earth tipped and pressed into a rising ridge
abstract.cn: 一车车土倒下、压实，垒成越来越高的土埂

examples.en: The train ran along an embankment above the flooded fields.
examples.cn: 火车沿着高出淹水田地的路堤行驶。

examples.en: The embankment held the river back from the sleeping village.
examples.cn: 堤岸把河水挡在熟睡的村庄之外。

examples.en: They built the embankment from three hundred carts of earth.
examples.cn: 他们用三百车土筑起了这道堤。

dict_mnemonic.text: embankment ＝ em-（使进入…状态）＋ bank（土埂；岸，古诺斯语 banki）＋ -ment（名词后缀，表行为或结果）＝「筑起来的土埂」。动词 embank 筑堤围住，同族 bank 岸、堤，banking 筑堤、银行业，sandbank 沙洲。两类实物：路堤 a railway embankment 铁路路堤、an embankment of earth 土堤；防洪堤 a river embankment 河堤、the embankment collapsed 堤岸垮了。也可指工程本身，不可数：embankment took the whole summer 筑堤花了整个夏天。近义 levee 多指大河防洪堤，dyke 多指挡海水的堤堰，mound 只是土堆，不一定挡水。注意与 embark（上船；着手）拼写相近，embarkment 不是英语词，上船的名词是 embarkation。

root: 古诺斯语 banki（土埂）→ 中古英语 banke → bank ＋ em-（使）＋ -ment（名词后缀）→ embankment（堤岸；筑堤）

sensesIntro.en: Three views of one ridge of earth: a railway on its top, a river at its foot and the carts that raised it.
sensesIntro.cn: 一条土埂的三个视角：顶上的铁路、脚下的河水，以及把它垒起来的一车车土。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long earth ridge with a railway on top and a river pushing at its foot
core.cn: 核心意象：一条长长的土埂，顶上铺着铁轨，河水在埂脚推着

branches.en: Earth raised to carry a road.
branches.cn: 垒高的土用来承载道路。

branches.en: Earth raised to hold back water.
branches.cn: 垒高的土用来挡住水。

branches.en: The work of raising the earth.
branches.cn: 把土垒起来的工程。

branches.en: Both are a long ridge with two slopes.
branches.cn: 两者都是带两个斜面的长埂。

branches.en: Both answer the pressure of a river.
branches.cn: 两者都回应河水的压力。

intro.en: Embankment is em- plus bank plus -ment; the verb embank drops -ment, and bank gives sandbank and banking.
intro.cn: embankment 由 em- 加 bank 加 -ment 组成；动词 embank 去掉 -ment，bank 给出 sandbank 与 banking。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic, not Latin: Old Norse banki means a ridge of earth; em- and -ment are the French and Latin layers added in English.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是日耳曼语而非拉丁语：古诺斯语 banki 意为土埂；em- 与 -ment 是英语中加上的法语与拉丁语层。

definition_zh: n. 禁运；禁止贸易；封港；（新闻）禁止发表令 v. 对…实行禁运；禁止发表
definition_en: an official order that stops trade or the publication of news
core_image: 港口入口横着一道红白栏杆，一艘满载的货轮停在栏杆外，船钟响了也没人放行
scene: 港口入口横着一道红白栏杆，一艘满载的货轮停在栏杆外，船员把缆绳收了又放。An embargo kept the cargo ship outside the harbour for eleven days.
sceneCN: 这里 embargo 指「封港禁航」（第 2 个义项：禁止船只进出港口）；句意是禁运令让货轮在港外停了十一天。

pos.zh: 禁运；禁止贸易；（新闻）禁止发表令
对…实行禁运；禁止（船只）进出港；禁止发表

senses.title: An official ban on trade
senses.definition: an official order that stops trade with a country
senses.definitionCN: （名词）禁止与某国贸易的官方命令
senses.example: The council imposed an arms embargo on the region.
senses.exampleCN: 理事会对该地区实施了武器禁运。
senses.why: A customs stamp on a paper that closes a whole border to goods
senses.whyCN: 文件上的一枚关员印章，把整条边界对货物关闭

senses.title: A ban on ships
senses.definition: an order that prevents ships from entering or leaving a port
senses.definitionCN: （名词）禁止船只进出港口的命令
senses.example: An embargo kept the cargo ship outside the harbour for eleven days.
senses.exampleCN: 禁运令让货轮在港外停了十一天。
senses.why: A red and white bar across a harbour mouth with a loaded ship waiting outside
senses.whyCN: 港口入口横着一道红白栏杆，一艘满载的船在外面等

senses.title: A ban on publishing news
senses.definition: an instruction that news must not be published before a set time
senses.definitionCN: （名词）约定时间之前不得发表新闻的指令
senses.example: The results are under embargo until the journal publishes on Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 结果在期刊周五发表之前禁止对外披露。
senses.why: A journalist holding a finished story until the agreed hour strikes
senses.whyCN: 记者把写好的稿子按住，直到约定的钟点敲响

intro.en: Embargo comes from Spanish embargar, to seize or to bar, built from em- and barra meaning a bar; the word entered English through the seizure of ships.
intro.cn: embargo 来自西班牙语 embargar（扣押；阻拦），由 em- 与 barra（栏杆）构成；这个词经扣押船只之事进入英语。

items.en: Barra means a bar or a rod, the root behind bar and barrier.
items.cn: barra 意为条或杆，是 bar 与 barrier 背后的词根。

items.en: Embargar means to seize or to hinder, from em- plus barra.
items.cn: embargar 意为扣押或阻拦，由 em- 加 barra 构成。

items.en: Embargo is the noun, a seizure or an arrest of ships.
items.cn: embargo 是名词，指扣押或对船只的扣留。

items.en: English borrows embargo in the 1590s for an order stopping ships from leaving port.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪 90 年代借入 embargo，指禁止船只离港的命令。

items.en: Embargo extends to a formal ban on trade with a whole country.
items.cn: embargo 扩展到对整国贸易的正式禁令。

dict_mnemonic.text: embargo ＝ em-（使进入）＋ barra（杆；栏，西班牙语）＝「横上一道杆」。复数 embargoes 或 embargos，动词三单 embargoes、过去式与过去分词 embargoed、现在分词 embargoing。同根 bar 条、阻拦，barrier 障碍，barricade 路障，barrage 弹幕。三层用法：贸易禁运 an arms embargo 武器禁运、an oil embargo 石油禁运、impose an embargo 实施禁运、lift an embargo 解除禁运；封港 an embargo on shipping 禁航令；新闻禁止发表 under embargo 在禁止发表期内、embargoed until Friday 周五前不得发表。近义 ban 泛指禁令，blockade 指用武力封锁，sanction 指惩罚性制裁；embargo 特指官方禁止贸易或禁止发表。注意与 embark（上船；着手）只差一个字母。

root: 拉丁语 barra（杆）→ 西班牙语 em-（使）＋ barra → embargar（扣押；阻拦）→ embargo（禁运）

dict_mnemonic.text: embark ＝ em-（使进入）＋ bark／barque（小船，拉丁 barca）＝「把自己放进船里」。名词 embarkation 上船、装载；反义 disembark 下船、disembarkation 上岸；同根 barque 三桅帆船。两个方向：上船 embark at Southampton 在南安普敦登船、embark for Europe 乘船去欧洲、passengers embark 旅客登船；着手 embark on a journey 开始一段旅程、embark on a career 投身一份事业、embark upon a project 着手一个项目。及物用法较少：embark passengers 让旅客上船、embark cargo 装货。介词固定用 on 或 upon，不用 in。近义 board 侧重登上交通工具，undertake 侧重承担责任，launch 侧重启动；embark 强调离岸启程的开端感。注意与 embargo（禁运）只差一个字母，embarkment 不是英语词。

definition_zh: 使尴尬；使难堪；使为难；阻碍
definition_en: to make someone feel ashamed or awkward; to cause difficulty for someone or something
core_image: 被一道看不见的栏杆围住，进退都不自在
scene: 台上是一段长长的沉默，年轻演讲者握着稿子的手停在半空，脸一下红到耳根。The long silence embarrassed the young speaker.
sceneCN: 这里 embarrass 是「使难堪」（第 1 个义项：让人感到羞愧不自在）；句意是长时间的沉默让年轻演讲者很难堪。

pos.zh: 使尴尬；使难堪；使为难

senses.title: To make someone feel awkward
senses.definition: to make a person feel ashamed, nervous or socially uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 让人感到羞愧、紧张或在人前不自在
senses.example: The long silence embarrassed the young speaker.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间的沉默让年轻演讲者很难堪。
senses.why: The old verb meant to block or entangle, so the core picture is being caught behind a barrier with no easy way out, which is exactly how social awkwardness feels.
senses.whyCN: 这个古老动词原本表示阻挡、缠住，核心画面是被栏杆困住、找不到出口，这正是社交尴尬的感受。

senses.title: To put someone in a difficult position
senses.definition: to cause problems or difficulties for a person or organization
senses.definitionCN: 给个人或机构造成麻烦与困难
senses.example: The question embarrassed the government.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题让政府很为难。
senses.why: Being blocked is not only social but practical, so the same verb describes a person or body trapped by an awkward problem.
senses.whyCN: 被挡住不只是社交上的事，也可能是实际处境，于是同一个动词也形容人或机构被难题困住。

senses.title: To hamper or obstruct, in older use
senses.definition: to hinder or obstruct movement or progress, an older and now rare sense
senses.definitionCN: 阻碍移动或进展，这是较旧且罕见的义项
senses.example: Fallen trees embarrassed the advance of the column.
senses.exampleCN: 倒下的树木阻碍了队伍前进。
senses.why: The earliest sense is physical obstruction, and the social sense grew from it; the old meaning survives mainly in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 最早的意思就是物理上的阻挡，社交义由此长出；旧义如今主要残留在正式书面语里。

intro.en: Embarrass came through French from a verb meaning to bar in, so its oldest picture is a barrier, not a blush.

items.en: Embarrasser carried the sense of blocking or entangling.
items.cn: embarrasser 带有阻挡、缠住的意思。

items.en: English borrowed the verb first for physical hindrance.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入该动词，最初指物理上的阻碍。

items.en: The social sense of making someone uncomfortable became common.

items.cn: 今天尴尬义占主导，阻碍义则少见且正式。

intro.en: Embezzlement comes from Anglo-French embesiler, to steal or to make away with, built from en- and besiler, to maltreat; -ment turns the verb into the crime.
intro.cn: embezzlement 来自盎格鲁法语 embesiler（偷走；使消失），由 en- 与 besiler（虐待；损坏）构成；-ment 把动词变成罪名。

items.en: En- means in or into, and becomes em- before b and p.
items.cn: en- 意为进入，在 b 与 p 前变成 em-。

items.en: Besiler means to maltreat or to destroy, the older sense behind this family.
items.cn: besiler 意为虐待或损坏，是这组词更早的意义来源。

items.en: Embesiler means to steal or to make away with goods entrusted to you.
items.cn: embesiler 意为偷走或使受托财物消失。

items.en: English takes embezzle in the 1400s, at first meaning to waste or to squander.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪吸收 embezzle，起初意为浪费或挥霍。

items.en: Embezzlement appears as the noun for the crime of taking entrusted money.
items.cn: embezzlement 作为窃取受托钱财之罪的名词出现。

items.en: Embezzler becomes the standard term in court reports and banking law.
items.cn: embezzler 成为法庭报道与银行法中的标准用词。

note.en: Embezzlement, embezzle and embezzler form one family; the nearest crime words are misappropriation and peculation.
note.cn: embezzlement、embezzle 与 embezzler 构成同一词族；最接近的罪名用词是 misappropriation 与 peculation。

dict_mnemonic.text: embezzlement ＝ embezzle（挪用；贪污）＋ -ment（名词后缀，表行为或结果）＝「挪用这件事」。动词 embezzle，行为人 embezzler 挪用公款者。不可数为主，指具体案件时可数：a case of embezzlement 一桩挪用案、two embezzlements 两起挪用。常见搭配 embezzlement of public funds 挪用公款、charged with embezzlement 被控挪用、convicted of embezzlement 被判挪用罪、commit embezzlement 实施挪用。词源是盎格鲁法语 embesiler「偷走受托财物」，早期英语里 embezzle 还指挥霍浪费。近义 misappropriation 泛指把款项用于不当用途，peculation 是法律语体的挪用公款，fraud 泛指欺诈；embezzlement 的关键是钱本来合法地交到你手上。注意与 embellishment（润色）拼写相近。

root: 盎格鲁法语 en-（进入）＋ besiler（损坏）→ embesiler（偷走受托财物）→ embezzle（挪用）＋ -ment → embezzlement

intro.en: Embody is em- plus body, from Old English bodig; to embody is to give an idea a body so that it can be seen and touched.
intro.cn: embody 由 em- 加 body 组成，body 来自古英语 bodig；embody 就是给理念一个身体，让它能被看见、被摸到。

items.en: Bodig means the trunk or the whole physical frame, and gives English body.
items.cn: bodig 意为躯干或整个身体，给出英语 body。

items.en: Body extends to a group of people and to the main part of a text.
items.cn: body 扩展到一群人，也扩展到文本的主体。

items.en: Embody appears in the 1540s, meaning to invest a spirit with a body.
items.cn: embody 出现于 16 世纪 40 年代，意为给灵魂赋予身体。

items.en: Embodiment is formed for the thing in which a quality is made visible.
items.cn: embodiment 构成，指某种品质得以显现的载体。

items.en: Embody is used for a person or work that perfectly represents an ideal.
items.cn: embody 用于指完美代表某种理想的人或作品。

items.en: Legal writing uses embody for including a rule inside a larger document.
items.cn: 法律文字用 embody 指把一条规则纳入更大的文件。

note.en: Embody, embodiment and bodily share the Germanic root bodig, a physical frame; incarnate and incorporate are the nearest synonyms.
note.cn: embody、embodiment 与 bodily 共享日耳曼词根 bodig（身体）；incarnate 与 incorporate 是最接近的同义词。

dict_mnemonic.text: embody ＝ em-（使进入）＋ body（身体，古英语 bodig）＝「给理念一副身体」。三单 embodies，过去式与过去分词 embodied，现在分词 embodying；名词 embodiment 体现、化身；同族 body 身体、主体，bodily 身体的，bodiless 无实体的，disembody 使脱离肉体。三类用法：体现抽象 embody a principle 体现一条原则、embody the spirit of 体现…的精神、embody an ideal 体现一种理想；化身 she embodies patience 她是耐心的化身；纳入 embody in law 写进法律、the treaty embodies the clause 条约纳入该条款。近义 incarnate 强调赋予血肉形体，personify 强调某人恰是某品质的代表，incorporate 强调并入整体；embody 兼有使可见与纳入两义。注意与 embolden（使有胆量）拼写相近。

definition_zh: v. 使凸出；压凸；以浮雕装饰；压印（凸字）
definition_en: to decorate a surface with a design that stands out in relief
core_image: 一张厚纸被钢模压过，纸面鼓起一行字母，指尖摸过去能读出凸起，背面却是凹进去的
scene: 印厂的钢模合拢又打开，一张厚纸被压过，纸面鼓起一行字母，指尖摸过去能读出凸起。The press embossed the title in raised letters on the cover.
sceneCN: 这里 emboss 指「压印凸字」（第 2 个义项：把字母压成凸起以便触摸）；句意是压印机在封面上把书名压成凸字。

dict_mnemonic.text: emboss ＝ em-（使进入）＋ boss（凸饰；鼓包，古法语 boce）＝「让鼓包凸出来」。三单 embosses，过去式与过去分词 embossed，现在分词 embossing；名词 embossment 凸纹装饰，工具名 embosser 压凸器；同根 boss 在建筑里指圆形凸饰，不是老板那个义项。三类用法：压凸图案 emboss a pattern 压出图案、emboss a logo 压出标志；凸字 embossed in gold 烫金凸字、embossed paper 压纹纸、embossed Braille 凸点盲文；皮革金属 embossed leather 压花皮革。形容词 embossed 最常见：an embossed cover 压凸封面。近义 engrave 是刻进去（凹），imprint 与 stamp 是压上标记，不一定凸起；emboss 的关键是凸出来、摸得到，与 deboss（压凹）正好相反。

root: 古法语 boce（隆起；鼓包）→ boss（凸饰）＋ em-（使）→ emboss（使凸出；压凸）

sensesIntro.en: Three raised surfaces: letters standing up on paper, dots a fingertip can read and a vine pattern pressed into leather.
sensesIntro.cn: 三种凸起的表面：纸上鼓起的字母、指尖能读出的凸点，以及压进皮革的藤纹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steel die closing on thick paper until a line of letters rises on the face
core.cn: 核心意象：钢模在厚纸上合拢，直到纸面鼓起一行字母

branches.en: A design stands out from a surface.
branches.cn: 纹样从表面凸出来。

branches.en: Letters can be read by touch.
branches.cn: 字母能被指尖读出。

branches.en: Leather or metal carries raised ornament.
branches.cn: 皮革或金属带上凸饰。

branches.en: Both raise the surface above the flat.
branches.cn: 两者都让表面高出平面。

branches.en: Both are ornament made by pressure.
branches.cn: 两者都是靠压力做出的装饰。

intro.en: Emboss is em- plus boss; -ment gives embossment, -er gives embosser, and de- gives the opposite deboss.
intro.cn: emboss 由 em- 加 boss 组成；-ment 给出 embossment，-er 给出 embosser，de- 给出反义词 deboss。

latinIntro.en: The root is Old French boce, a swelling; Latin tuber also means a bump and gives tubercle, while the carving word engrave comes from Old English grafan.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是古法语 boce（隆起）；拉丁语 tuber 也意为鼓包，给出 tubercle，而雕刻词 engrave 来自古英语 grafan。

definition_zh: 拥抱；欣然接受；包含；包围
definition_en: to hold someone closely in the arms; to accept an idea willingly; to include or contain
core_image: 两条手臂合拢，把一个人或一个念头整个圈进来
scene: 车站重逢，两人隔着人群张开手臂。They embraced at the station after two years apart.
sceneCN: 这里 embrace 是「拥抱」（第 1 个义项：用双臂抱紧某人）；句意是分别两年后他们在车站拥抱。

pos.zh: 拥抱；欣然接受；包含
拥抱

senses.title: To hold someone in the arms
senses.definition: to put your arms around someone and hold them closely
senses.definitionCN: 用双臂环住某人并抱紧
senses.example: They embraced at the station after two years apart.
senses.exampleCN: 分别两年后他们在车站拥抱。
senses.why: The French source joins in- with brace, an arm, so the word's body is literally putting arms around someone.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源把 in-（在内）与 brace（手臂）结合，所以这个词的身体动作字面就是「把手臂环上去」。

senses.title: To accept an idea willingly
senses.definition: to accept a belief, change or opportunity with enthusiasm
senses.definitionCN: 热情地接受某种观念、变化或机会
senses.example: The company embraced the new technology.
senses.exampleCN: 公司欣然接受了这项新技术。
senses.why: An idea can be taken into the arms the way a person is, so embracing a plan means drawing it close instead of pushing it away.
senses.whyCN: 观念也能像人一样被抱进怀里，所以 embrace a plan 就是把计划拉近，而不是推开。

senses.title: To include or contain
senses.definition: to include something as part of a larger whole
senses.definitionCN: 把某物作为更大整体的一部分包含进来
senses.example: The course embraces both theory and practice.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课兼顾理论与实践。
senses.why: Arms that close around a group enclose everything inside, so the verb extends from hugging a person to containing a range of things.
senses.whyCN: 手臂合拢会把一群东西都圈在里面，于是这个动词从抱人扩展到涵盖一系列事物。

intro.en: Embrace came from Old French, where the word for arm supplied the picture of arms closing around something.
intro.cn: embrace 来自古法语，其中表示「手臂」的词提供了双臂合拢的画面。

items.en: Bracchium meant the forearm or arm.
items.cn: bracchium 意为前臂或手臂。

items.en: Brace meant an arm, and the verb embracier meant to put arms around.
items.cn: brace 意为手臂，动词 embracier 意为用双臂环抱。

items.en: English borrowed embrace in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 embrace。

items.en: The figurative sense of accepting an idea appeared.
items.cn: 表示接受某种观念的比喻义出现。

items.en: The verb now covers hugging, accepting and including.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个动词涵盖拥抱、接受与包含。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the arm root; the near-meaning group separates a hug, acceptance and inclusion.
note.cn: 形近组沿着「手臂」词根展开；近义组区分拥抱、接受与包含。

entries.definition: An ornament worn around the wrist, from the arm root.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「手链」，词根仍是「手臂」。

entries.definition: A support or pair, from the same Old French arm word.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「支架、一对」，源自古法语的手臂词。

entries.definition: The act of embracing, a rare noun.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为「拥抱、接受」，较少见。

entries.definition: To hold someone closely, the plain everyday verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「拥抱」，是最日常的说法。

entries.definition: To agree to take something offered.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「接受」，对应本词的观念义。

entries.definition: To have something as part of a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「包含」，对应本词的涵盖义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks read embrace as arms closing in, then let the same circle take in ideas and whole ranges.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 embrace 读成双臂合拢，再让同一个圆圈把观念与整片范围都圈进来。

normal.en: Em- plus brace, an arm: put arms around.
normal.cn: em- 加 brace（手臂）：把手臂环上去。

normal.en: A warm embrace is the plain physical sense.
normal.cn: warm embrace 就是最朴素的拥抱义。

normal.en: To embrace change is to hold it close.
normal.cn: embrace change 就是把变化抱近。

normal.en: A course that embraces theory and practice contains both.
normal.cn: embrace 两者的课程把二者都包含进来。

normal.en: Bracelet shares the same arm root.
normal.cn: bracelet 与本词共享「手臂」词根。

abstract.en: Picture two arms drawing a circle around a person or a plan.
abstract.cn: 想象两条手臂在一个人或一个计划周围画出一个圆圈。

abstract.en: The same gesture means welcome, agreement and containment.
abstract.cn: 同一个动作同时表示欢迎、同意与容纳。

abstract.en: Embrace is a hug that learned to hold ideas.
abstract.cn: embrace 就是一个学会了抱想法的拥抱。

examples.en: They embraced at the station after two years apart.
examples.cn: 分别两年后他们在车站拥抱。

examples.en: The company embraced the new technology.
examples.cn: 公司欣然接受了这项新技术。

examples.en: The course embraces both theory and practice.
examples.cn: 这门课兼顾理论与实践。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因不来死」——久别重逢，抱紧一点才不松开

root: 经古法语 embracier 借入，由 em-（在内）加 brace（手臂）构成；brace 源自拉丁语 bracchium（手臂）。

sensesIntro.en: Embrace begins with arms around a person, then draws ideas close, then encloses a whole range.
sensesIntro.cn: embrace 先用双臂抱住一个人，再把观念拉近，最后把一整片范围圈进来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two arms drawing a closed circle around something.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条手臂合拢，把某物圈成一个闭合的圆。

branches.en: THE HUG: two people closing the circle.
branches.cn: 拥抱线：两个人把圆圈合上。

branches.en: THE IDEA: a plan drawn into the arms.
branches.cn: 观念线：把计划拉进怀里。

branches.en: THE RANGE: a whole set held inside the circle.
branches.cn: 范围线：把一整组事物圈在里面。

branches.en: BODY AND MIND: the same gesture welcomes a person and a thought.
branches.cn: 身与心：同一个动作既欢迎人，也欢迎想法。

branches.en: HOLD AND CONTAIN: arms that hug also enclose.
branches.cn: 抱与容：会拥抱的手臂也会围住。

intro.en: Embrace is a French borrowing built on brace, arm; English then added -ment and -able to make rare nouns and adjectives.
intro.cn: embrace 是建立在 brace（手臂）之上的法语借词；英语后来又加 -ment 与 -able 造出少见的名词和形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin bracchium, arm, is the recorded root behind the French word brace.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 bracchium（手臂）是法语 brace 背后有记录的词根。

items.meaning: he does, or more than one

derivatives.zh: 可拥抱的；可接受的（较少见）

definition_zh: 胚胎；（事物的）雏形；胚
definition_en: the unborn or newly developing young of an organism, or the earliest form of something
core_image: 一粒种子被切开，里面蜷着一条极小的根与芽，整个未来的植株已经按比例缩小藏在这里
scene: 在植物实验室里，技术员切开一枚种子说：The embryo inside the seed already has a tiny root and shoot.
sceneCN: 这里 embryo 指「种子内处于早期发育阶段的胚」（第 3 个义项：植物种子中的胚）；句意是种子里的胚已经有一条微小的根与芽。

pos.zh: 胚胎；胚；雏形；（事物的）初期形态

senses.title: The developing young of an animal
senses.definition: the unborn or newly developing young of an animal
senses.definitionCN: 动物未出生或刚发育的幼体
senses.example: The embryo implants in the womb about a week after fertilization.
senses.exampleCN: 受精约一周后，胚胎着床于子宫。
senses.why: Greek embryon named the young one still forming inside, so the noun points at the organism before it has taken shape.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 embryon 指在里面仍在形成的幼体，因此这个名词指尚未成形时的生物体。

senses.title: A human embryo in its early stage
senses.definition: a human organism in the first weeks after fertilization
senses.definitionCN: 受精后最初数周的人类生物体
senses.example: The human embryo is called a fetus after the eighth week.
senses.exampleCN: 人类胚胎在第八周之后被称为胎儿。
senses.why: Medicine needs a boundary, so embryo marks the early weeks before the fetal stage begins.
senses.whyCN: 医学需要一条界线，因此 embryo 标记胎儿阶段开始之前的最初数周。

senses.title: The plant embryo inside a seed
senses.definition: the young plant contained within a seed
senses.definitionCN: 包含在种子内的幼小植株
senses.example: The embryo inside the seed already has a tiny root and shoot.
senses.exampleCN: 种子里的胚已经有一条微小的根与芽。
senses.why: Plants package the young plant inside a seed, and botany uses the same noun for that dormant form.
senses.whyCN: 植物把幼株包在种子里，植物学用同一个名词指这种休眠形态。

senses.title: The earliest form of something
senses.definition: the beginning or germ of something that will develop further
senses.definitionCN: 将进一步发展之物的开端或雏形
senses.example: The first sketch was the embryo of the finished building.
senses.exampleCN: 第一幅草图是这座建成建筑的前身。
senses.why: Because an embryo contains the whole future in miniature, the noun extends to any early germ of a larger thing.
senses.whyCN: 因为胚胎以缩小的形式包含整个未来，这个名词便延伸到任何较大事物的早期雏形。

senses.title: An embryo in assisted reproduction
senses.definition: an embryo produced and transferred in fertility treatment
senses.definitionCN: 生育治疗中培育并移植的胚胎
senses.example: The clinic transferred one embryo and froze the others.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所移植了一个胚胎，把其余的冷冻起来。
senses.why: Reproductive technology makes the embryo an object handled outside the body, giving the noun a clinical sense.
senses.whyCN: 生殖技术使胚胎成为在体外被操作的对象，使这个名词获得临床义。

senses.title: An embryo as a specimen
senses.definition: a preserved or staged embryo used for study
senses.definitionCN: 用于研究而保存或分期的胚胎
senses.example: The collection holds embryos at every stage of development.
senses.exampleCN: 这批藏品保存着每个发育阶段的胚胎。
senses.why: In a laboratory the embryo becomes a specimen with a stage number, a thing to be compared rather than a future animal.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室里，胚胎变成带分期编号的标本，是被比较的对象，而非未来的动物。

senses.title: The embryo contrasted with the larva
senses.definition: the developmental stage before hatching, as distinct from a free-living larva
senses.definitionCN: 孵化之前的发育阶段，与自由生活的幼虫相对
senses.example: The embryo develops inside the egg before the larva emerges.
senses.exampleCN: 胚胎在卵内发育，之后幼虫才出来。
senses.why: Zoology separates stages by whether the young is still enclosed, and embryo marks the enclosed phase.
senses.whyCN: 动物学按幼体是否仍被包裹来划分阶段，embryo 标记被包裹的阶段。

senses.title: The germ of a plan or design
senses.titleCN: 计划或设计的最初构想
senses.definition: an early idea from which a plan or work may grow
senses.definitionCN: 计划或作品可能由此生长的最初想法
senses.example: The idea remained an embryo for years before anyone funded it.
senses.exampleCN: 这个想法多年只是雏形，直到有人资助。
senses.why: The biological image gives the noun a figurative life: a plan can be pregnant with a future it has not yet shown.
senses.whyCN: 生物意象给这个名词以比喻生命：一个计划可以孕育着尚未显露的未来。

intro.en: Embryo comes from Greek embryon, a young one still forming, built from en- in and bryein to swell; Latin and English adopted it as a scientific noun.
intro.cn: embryo 来自希腊 embryon「仍在形成的幼体」，由 en-「在内」与 bryein「膨胀」构成；拉丁语与英语把它作为科学名词吸收。

items.en: Embryon meant a young one, and also a swelling; the word pictured life growing inside a enclosing body.
items.cn: embryon 意为幼体，也指肿块；这个词描绘生命在有包裹的身体内生长。

items.en: En- meant in and bryein meant to swell or be full; the compound's literal sense is swelling within.
items.cn: en- 意为「在内」，bryein 意为「膨胀、充满」；复合词的字面义是「在里面膨胀」。

items.en: Latin took the Greek noun as embryo and used it in learned writing for the unborn young.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这一希腊名词吸收为 embryo，在学术写作中指未出生的幼体。

items.en: English embryo appeared in the sixteenth century, first in learned and medical contexts.
items.cn: 英语 embryo 在 16 世纪出现，最初用于学术与医学语境。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the noun was also used for the early form of a thing, a usage that persists in modern writing.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，这个名词也用于指事物的早期形态，这一用法在现代写作中延续。

items.en: Source uncertain as to the root: the deeper origin of bryein is not established, so any Indo-European base offered is a reconstruction; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（bryein 词根存疑、年代为约数）：bryein 的更深来源未得到证明，凡为其给出的印欧语基均属重构形式；英语首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same embryo stock; group two holds stages and near terms in developmental biology.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 embryo 词族的词；第二组是发育生物学中的阶段与近义术语。

entries.definition: Relating to an embryo or to an early stage; it describes, while embryo names the object.
entries.definitionCN: 与胚胎或早期阶段有关的形容词；它作描述，而 embryo 指对象。

entries.definition: The study of embryos; it names a science, not the organism.
entries.definitionCN: 研究胚胎的学科；它指科学，而非生物体。

entries.definition: A rarer adjective for embryonic tissue, used mainly in pathology and anatomy.
entries.definitionCN: 较少见的形容词，指胚胎组织，主要用于病理学与解剖学。

entries.definition: The nourishing tissue inside a seed; it surrounds the plant embryo but is not the embryo itself.
entries.definitionCN: 种子内提供营养的组织；它包围植物胚，但本身不是胚。

entries.definition: The unborn young after the embryonic stage; the two nouns mark successive phases.
entries.definitionCN: 胚胎阶段之后未出生的幼体；两个名词标记相继阶段。

entries.definition: An independent young form that hatches and feeds itself, unlike an embryo still enclosed.
entries.definitionCN: 孵化后独立取食的幼体形态，与仍被包裹的胚胎不同。

entries.definition: The structure that holds the plant embryo with its food supply; the embryo is inside the seed.
entries.definitionCN: 包含植物胚与养分供应的结构；胚在种子内部。

entries.definition: The earliest stage from which something may develop; it is the figurative counterpart of embryo.
entries.definitionCN: 某物可能由此发展的最早阶段；是 embryo 的比喻对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: En- in plus bryein swell: life swelling inside a wrapping.
normal.cn: en-「在内」加 bryein「膨胀」：生命在包裹内膨胀。

normal.en: The family runs embryo, embryonic, embryology, embryologist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 embryo、embryonic、embryology、embryologist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: human embryo, plant embryo, embryo transfer, embryo sac.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：人类胚胎、植物胚、胚胎移植、胚囊。

normal.en: The timeline is embryo, then fetus, then birth.
normal.cn: 时间线是胚胎、胎儿、出生。

normal.en: In seeds the embryo waits, tiny but complete in outline.
normal.cn: 在种子里，胚静静等待，微小却轮廓完整。

abstract.en: Picture a seed cut open to reveal a miniature plant.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子被切开，露出一株缩小的植株。

abstract.en: Picture a blueprint folded small enough to fit in a pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象一张蓝图折得小到能放进口袋。

abstract.en: Picture a whole tree sleeping inside one hard shell.
abstract.cn: 想象整棵树睡在一枚硬壳里。

examples.en: The embryo divides rapidly in the first days after fertilization.
examples.cn: 受精后的最初几天，胚胎迅速分裂。

examples.en: Botanists distinguish the embryo from the surrounding food tissue.
examples.cn: 植物学家把胚与周围的营养组织区分开。

examples.en: The novel was still an embryo when the war began.
examples.cn: 战争开始时，这部小说还只是雏形。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「em 在内 + bryo 膨胀」——在里面膨胀生长的幼体 → 胚胎、雏形

root: 希腊 embryon「仍在形成的幼体；肿块」= en-「在内」+ bryein「膨胀」，经拉丁 embryo 进入英语；bryein 更深词根不确定，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one noun from an animal's developing young to a human stage, a seed's plant, a figurative germ, a clinical object, a museum specimen, a zoological phase and the first form of a plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一个名词从动物发育中的幼体走向人类阶段、种子里的植株、比喻的雏形、临床对象、博物馆标本、动物学阶段，最后走向计划的最初形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seed opened to show a tiny plant that already carries the whole future in outline.
core.cn: 核心意象：一粒种子被打开，露出一株已以轮廓携带全部未来的小植株。

branches.en: BIOLOGICAL YOUNG: animal, human and plant embryos are the same stage in different containers.
branches.cn: 生物学幼体：动物、人类与植物胚是不同容器中的同一阶段。

branches.en: EARLIEST FORM: anything larger begins as an embryo of itself.
branches.cn: 最初形态：任何更大的事物都以自身的胚胎形态开始。

branches.en: OBJECT OF HANDLING: clinics transfer embryos, museums stage them as specimens.
branches.cn: 被操作的对象：诊所移植胚胎，博物馆把它分期为标本。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: the embryo ends where the free-living larva or fetus begins.
branches.cn: 边界：胚胎在自由生活幼虫或胎儿开始处结束。

branches.en: UNREALIZED FUTURE: the noun names something whose future is still folded inside it.
branches.cn: 未实现的未来：这个名词指未来仍折叠在其内部的事物。

definition_zh: 出现；浮现；显露；脱颖而出
definition_en: to come out from a hidden place; to become known; to come into existence; to survive a difficult period
core_image: 水面下的一团影子慢慢升起，终于露出水面
scene: 云层裂开，太阳从背后露出边缘。The sun emerged from behind the clouds.
sceneCN: 这里 emerge 是「露出、出现」（第 1 个义项：从遮蔽处出来）；句意是太阳从云层后露出。

pos.zh: 出现；浮现；显露；脱颖而出

senses.title: To come out from a hidden place
senses.definition: to move out of water, darkness or another covering and become visible
senses.definitionCN: 从水中、暗处或其他遮盖物里出来并变得可见
senses.example: The sun emerged from behind the clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳从云层后露出。
senses.why: The Latin verb joins e-, out, with mergere, to dip or sink, so the core picture is something rising out of the water into view.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词由 e-（向外）与 mergere（浸入、下沉）组合，核心画面就是某物从水里升起、露出水面。

senses.title: To become known
senses.definition: to become known or apparent after being hidden or unclear
senses.definitionCN: 原本隐藏或不清晰的事情变得为人所知
senses.example: New facts emerged during the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 审判过程中有新的情况显露出来。
senses.why: Facts can rise out of obscurity just as an object rises out of water, so the physical surfacing becomes a metaphor for disclosure.
senses.whyCN: 事实能像物体升出水面一样从模糊中浮现，于是这个物理动作变成了「真相显露」的比喻。

senses.title: To come into existence
senses.definition: to begin to exist or become established
senses.definitionCN: 开始存在或逐渐确立
senses.example: A new industry emerged in the coastal city.
senses.exampleCN: 一座新兴产业在这座沿海城市兴起。
senses.why: What rises into view did not exist for the observer before, so emergence also names the birth of a thing or trend.
senses.whyCN: 对观察者来说，升起并进入视野的东西此前并不存在，所以 emergence 也用来命名事物或趋势的诞生。

senses.title: To survive a difficult period
senses.definition: to come out of a difficult experience in a new or stronger position
senses.definitionCN: 从艰难经历中走出来，处于新的或更强的位置
senses.example: The small firm emerged stronger after the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 危机之后这家小公司变得更强。
senses.why: Coming out of water is also coming out of danger, so the verb describes a person or group that survives a trial and steps into the open.
senses.whyCN: 从水里出来也意味着从危险中出来，所以这个动词形容人或群体熬过考验、走到开阔处。

intro.en: Emerge comes straight from Latin emergere, to rise out of a liquid.
intro.cn: emerge 直接来自拉丁语 emergere，意为从液体中升起。

items.en: Mergere meant to dip, plunge or sink.
items.cn: mergere 意为浸入、扎入或下沉。

items.en: With e-, out, the verb meant to rise out of water.
items.cn: 加上 e-（向外）后，动词意为从水中升起。

items.en: The participle described something coming up into view.
items.cn: 其分词形容某物升上来、进入视野。

items.en: English borrowed the verb for physical surfacing.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入该动词，表示物理上的浮出。

items.en: The sense widened to facts becoming known and new things coming into being.
items.cn: 词义扩大到事实显露与新事物产生。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the merge root and its derived nouns; the near-meaning group separates appearing, surfacing and arising.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 merge 词根及其派生名词展开；近义组区分出现、浮出水面与产生。

entries.definition: Newly appearing or developing.

entries.definition: To sink into or combine, from the same Latin verb without e-.

entries.definition: To become visible, often without effort.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「出现」，常不带努力感。

entries.definition: To come up to the top, literally or figuratively.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「浮出水面」，可实指也可比喻。

entries.definition: To begin to exist, especially of problems or situations.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「产生」，多用于问题或局面。

normal.en: A new market can emerge overnight.

normal.en: A team can emerge stronger from a crisis.
normal.cn: 一个团队能从危机中变得更强。

abstract.en: What was hidden becomes visible, and what did not exist begins to be.
abstract.cn: 藏着的东西变得可见，不存在的东西开始存在。

abstract.en: Emerge is a birth told as a surfacing.

definition_zh: 紧急情况；突发事件；急件
definition_en: a sudden dangerous situation that needs immediate action; used in such a situation
core_image: 平静的水面忽然炸开，所有人都得立刻行动
scene: 警报骤然响起，人群涌到安全通道口，却发现那里堆满了纸箱，谁也推不开那扇门。The emergency exit was blocked by boxes.
sceneCN: 这里 emergency 是「紧急情况」（第 1 个义项：需要立即处理的危险局面）；句意是紧急出口被箱子堵住了。

pos.zh: 紧急情况；突发事件
应急的；紧急的

senses.title: A sudden dangerous situation
senses.definition: a sudden serious event that requires immediate attention
senses.definitionCN: 突然发生、需要立即处理的严重事件
senses.example: The emergency exit was blocked by boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 紧急出口被箱子堵住了。
senses.why: The noun began as an unforeseen occurrence that suddenly rises up, so emergency is a situation that breaks through ordinary routine without warning.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词最早指突然「冒出来」的意外事件，所以 emergency 就是毫无预警地冲破日常秩序的处境。

senses.title: Used for such a situation
senses.definition: designed or kept for use in a sudden dangerous situation
senses.definitionCN: 为突发危险局面设计或保存的
senses.example: They kept an emergency fund for hard times.
senses.exampleCN: 他们存了一笔应急资金以备难关。
senses.why: A thing reserved for the sudden event borrows the event's name, so an exit, fund or room can all be called emergency.
senses.whyCN: 为突发状况预留的东西借用了状况的名字，所以出口、资金或房间都能用 emergency 作定语。

senses.title: An unforeseen occurrence, in older use
senses.definition: any unexpected event, an older and broader sense
senses.definitionCN: 任何未预料到的事件，是较旧且更宽的义项
senses.example: The diary records several emergencies of the voyage.
senses.exampleCN: 日记记下了航行中的几件意外。
senses.why: Before it specialised in danger, the word simply meant something that emerged unexpectedly, which is why old texts use it for any surprise.
senses.whyCN: 在专门表示危险之前，这个词只表示「意外冒出来的事」，所以旧文献里任何突发情况都能用它。

dict_mnemonic.text: emeritus ＝ e-（出）＋ meritus（挣得的，拉丁 merere「应得」的过去分词）＝「已服满役期、功成身退」。原是拉丁语，直接借入英语。拉丁式复数 emeriti（阳性或混合）、阴性单数 emerita、阴性复数 emeritae；英语也可写 emerituses。同根 merit 功绩、meritorious 有功的、demerit 过失、meritocracy 精英体制。用法：作形容词常后置 professor emeritus 荣誉退休教授，前置 emeritus professor 也常见，另有 emeritus status 荣誉退休身份、emeritus of history 历史学荣誉退休教授；作名词指人 an emeritus 一位荣誉退休者、the emeriti 全体荣誉退休人员。近义 retired 只说退休，honorary 指未经实际任职而授予的荣誉头衔；emeritus 特指实际任满、退休后保留原头衔。注意重音在第二音节。

root: 拉丁语 e-（出）＋ merere（应得）→ meritus（挣得的）→ emeritus（已服满役期的）→ 荣誉退休的

sensesIntro.en: Three signs of a title kept after service: one extra word on a door plate, a rank printed after the chair and a retired teacher who still marks one essay.
sensesIntro.cn: 役满之后保留头衔的三个标志：门牌上多出的一个词、印在讲席职称之后的职级，以及仍批一篇作文的退休教师。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door plate with one extra Latin word after the name and the same key on its board
core.cn: 核心意象：门牌上名字后面多了一个拉丁词，钥匙还挂在同一块木板上

branches.en: Service ended but the title stays.
branches.cn: 任期结束而头衔留下。

branches.en: The rank is written after the chair.
branches.cn: 职级写在讲席职称之后。

branches.en: A person holds this honoured status.
branches.cn: 一个人持有这份荣誉身份。

branches.en: Both mark a title that was earned.
branches.cn: 两者都标记一个挣得的头衔。

branches.en: Both keep a link after the work stops.
branches.cn: 两者都在工作停止后保留联系。

intro.en: Emeritus is e- plus meritus; the same root gives merit, meritorious, demerit and meritocracy.
intro.cn: emeritus 由 e- 加 meritus 组成；同一词根给出 merit、meritorious、demerit 与 meritocracy。

latinIntro.en: Latin merere means to deserve and meritus is its past participle; emeritus means having served out one time, first said of soldiers.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 merere 意为应得，meritus 是其过去分词；emeritus 意为已服满役期，最初用于士兵。

definition_zh: 移居出境；迁出；（总称）迁出者
definition_en: the act of leaving one's own country in order to settle in another, or the flow of people who do so
core_image: 码头边一只贴旧地址的行李箱，船票印着目的港，身后屋顶渐渐变成一条细线
scene: 小镇车站的告示牌下，年轻人提着行李与父母拥抱告别。Emigration from the region peaked in the years after the harvest failed.
sceneCN: 这里 emigration 指「离开本国到他国定居的行为」（第 1 个义项：迁出本国）；句意为这个地区的向外移民在歉收之后的几年里达到顶峰。图中可辨识物件：贴旧地址的行李箱、船票、远去的屋顶、告示牌。

pos.zh: 移居出境；迁出（不可数；指具体批次时可作可数）

senses.title: Leaving one's country to settle elsewhere
senses.definition: the act of departing from one's own country with the intention of living in another
senses.definitionCN: 离开本国并打算在他国生活的行为
senses.example: Emigration from the region peaked in the years after the harvest failed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区的向外移民在歉收之后的几年里达到顶峰。
senses.why: the prefix means out and the root means move, so emigration is the same crossing seen from the country people leave.
senses.whyCN: 前缀意为向外，词根意为迁移，因此 emigration 是从人们离开的国家看到的同一次越境。

senses.title: The volume of departures
senses.titleCN: 迁出人口的总量与流量
senses.definition: the number or flow of people leaving a country over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内离开一国的人数或人流
senses.example: Emigration doubled while the mines were closing.
senses.exampleCN: 矿区陆续关闭时，外迁人数翻了一番。
senses.why: the uncountable noun works like a quantity word, as with traffic or rainfall.
senses.whyCN: 这个不可数名词起数量词的作用，就像交通量或降雨量。

senses.title: A component of population change
senses.definition: the loss of people to other countries in the accounting of a population
senses.definitionCN: 在人口核算中流向其他国家而减少的人数
senses.example: Net emigration has kept the island's population flat.
senses.exampleCN: 净迁出使这个岛上的人口保持持平。
senses.why: demographers set emigration against immigration in the same ledger of gains and losses.
senses.whyCN: 人口学者把迁出与迁入放在同一本得失账簿的两侧。

senses.title: The departure side of a diaspora
senses.titleCN: 侨民社群形成时的离开一端
senses.definition: the outflow that builds communities of former residents abroad
senses.definitionCN: 在海外形成原居民社群的那股流出
senses.example: Emigration from the valley built three churches in the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 从这个山谷的向外移民在首都建起了三座教堂。
senses.why: the same movement that empties one place fills another, and the sending side keeps the name emigration.
senses.whyCN: 同一次移动使一处变空、另一处变满，输出方保留 emigration 这个名字。

senses.title: State policy on leaving
senses.definition: official rules that restrict, permit or encourage citizens to leave
senses.definitionCN: 限制、允许或鼓励公民离开的官方规定
senses.example: Emigration controls were relaxed only in the 1980s.
senses.exampleCN: 出境限制直到 20 世纪 80 年代才放宽。
senses.why: states can control exits as well as entries, so the word also names a policy field.
senses.whyCN: 国家既能管控入境也能管控出境，因此这个词也指一个政策领域。

senses.title: A historical wave
senses.definition: a distinct period in which large numbers of people left a country
senses.definitionCN: 大批人口离开某国的特定时期
senses.example: The great emigration of the 1840s changed the census for a century.
senses.exampleCN: 19 世纪 40 年代的移民大潮在一个世纪里改变了普查数据。
senses.why: a wave with a clear beginning and end becomes a countable historical event.
senses.whyCN: 起止清楚的浪潮会成为可计数的历史事件。

senses.title: Dispersal out of a population
senses.definition: the departure of individuals from a population into new areas
senses.definitionCN: 个体离开原种群进入新区域
senses.example: Emigration of young wolves keeps the pack from growing.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻狼群的迁出使这个群体不致过大。
senses.why: ecology names the outgoing half of dispersal with the same word, while immigration names the incoming half.
senses.whyCN: 生态学用同一个词命名扩散中出去的一半，而迁入命名进来的一半。

senses.title: Relocation to a lower-tax jurisdiction
senses.definition: the movement of wealthy individuals to a place with lower taxes
senses.definitionCN: 富裕个人迁往税负更低的地方
senses.example: Tax emigration drained the capital of its largest investors.
senses.exampleCN: 为避税而迁居使首都失去了最大的投资者。
senses.why: modern finance uses the word for money and its owners moving jurisdiction, echoing the older sense of leaving home.
senses.whyCN: 现代金融用这个词指资金及其所有者更换税区，回响着较早的「离乡」义。

intro.en: Emigration rests on Latin emigrare 'to move out', from e- or ex- 'out' plus migrare 'to migrate'. The English noun appeared in the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: emigration 源于拉丁 emigrare「迁出」，由 e- 或 ex-「向外」与 migrare「迁移」构成。英语名词出现于 17 世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Migrare meant 'to move, change one's dwelling'. Its own earlier origin is not established, and the root sometimes proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: migrare 意为「迁移、更换住所」。它更早的来源未得到证明，为其提出的词根属重构形式。

items.en: The prefix e- or ex- meant 'out of', and it marks the direction away from the starting country.
items.cn: 前缀 e- 或 ex- 意为「向外」，标记离开出发国的方向。

items.en: E- plus migrare gave emigrare 'to move out of a place', the mirror of immigrare 'to move into'.
items.cn: e- 加 migrare 构成 emigrare「迁出某地」，与 immigrare「迁入」正好互为镜像。

items.en: English formed emigration on the stem of emigrate in the seventeenth century, at first for any departure, later chiefly for departure across a national border.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪用 emigrate 的词干构成 emigration，最初泛指离开，后来主要指跨越国境的离开。

items.en: Nineteenth-century shipping records and twentieth-century border controls made the word a standard demographic measure, paired with immigration.
items.cn: 19 世纪的航运记录与 20 世纪的边境管控，使这个词成为标准的人口学指标，并与迁入配对使用。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin history of migrare is unsettled, and the earliest English citation is not precisely fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：migrare 在拉丁语之前的历史尚无定论，最早的英语书证也没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one holds the direction words that differ by one prefix; group two holds words for mass departure.
note.cn: 第一组是只差一个前缀的方向词；第二组是表示大规模离开的说法。

entries.definition: The same movement seen from the receiving country, with in- 'into' instead of e- 'out'.
entries.definitionCN: 同一移动从接收国看，前缀为「向内」而非「向外」。

entries.definition: Movement between places with no border specified; it covers internal moves, birds and even data.
entries.definitionCN: 未说明国境的位移；涵盖国内迁移、鸟类乃至数据。

entries.definition: The person who leaves; the action noun and the person noun are frequently swapped in careless speech.
entries.definitionCN: 离开的人；表动作的名词与表人的名词在随意言谈中常被互换。

entries.definition: To move into a country; the verb faces the destination, while emigrate faces the origin.
entries.definitionCN: 移入某国；这个动词朝向目的地，而迁出动词朝向原籍。

entries.definition: A large departure of people, often sudden and driven by hardship; it stresses the crowd rather than the legal act.
entries.definitionCN: 大批人的离开，常突然且由困境推动；强调人群而非法律行为。

entries.definition: The act of leaving a place, whether or not a new country is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 离开某地的行为，不论是否涉及新的国家。

entries.definition: Moving one's home or business to a new place; it is neutral about borders and motives.
entries.definitionCN: 把住所或企业迁到新地方；对国境与动机都保持中性。

entries.definition: The spreading of individuals away from a centre, used in ecology and in studies of migration.
entries.definitionCN: 个体从中心向外散开，用于生态学与迁移研究。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real prefix, the real root and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的前缀、真实的词根与真实的固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means out: emigration is the view from the door being closed behind you.
normal.cn: 前缀意为向外：向外移民就是从身后那扇关上的门看到的情形。

normal.en: The pair emigration and immigration differ only in the direction of the prefix.
normal.cn: 向外移民与向内移民这一对词，只差前缀的方向。

normal.en: The person noun ends in a suffix marking the one who acts.
normal.cn: 指人的名词以一个标记施动者的词尾收束。

normal.en: Fixed phrases such as emigration policy and net emigration belong to the statistical sense.
normal.cn: 外迁政策、净迁出这类固定搭配属于统计义。

normal.en: In ecology the same word names the outgoing half of dispersal.
normal.cn: 在生态学中，同一个词命名扩散中出去的那一半。

abstract.en: Picture a door closing on a room that will keep the shape of your absence.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门关上，房间里将一直留着你的空缺形状。

abstract.en: Picture a scale with departures on one pan and arrivals on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，一只盘放离开，另一只放到来。

abstract.en: Picture a map with an arrow pointing off its own edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，箭头指向地图边缘之外。

examples.en: Emigration rose when land prices collapsed in the countryside.
examples.cn: 乡村地价崩跌时，向外移民增加了。

examples.en: The government tried to slow emigration by offering rural loans.
examples.cn: 政府试图通过提供农村贷款来减缓向外移民。

examples.en: Emigration and immigration are recorded as separate lines in the census.
examples.cn: 在普查中，迁出与迁入被记为两条独立的项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一民·出去」——一批人离开本国到别处定居，就是向外移民

root: 拉丁 e- 或 ex-「向外」+ migrare「迁移」→ emigrare「迁出」；英语 emigration 于 17 世纪由 emigrate 的词干构成。migrare 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one departure: the act of leaving, the volume of leavers, the ledger entry, the founding of communities abroad, state policy, a historical wave, the outgoing half of biological dispersal and the flight of wealth to a lower-tax home.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一次离开展开：离开的行为、离开者的总量、账簿上的一行、海外社群的形成、国家政策、历史浪潮、生物扩散中出去的一半，以及财富迁往低税地的迁徙。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a suitcase on a quay, its old address label still stuck under the new one.
core.cn: 核心意象：码头上一只行李箱，旧地址标签仍压在新标签之下。

branches.en: LEAVING: the base act of departing in order to settle elsewhere.
branches.cn: 离开：为在别处定居而出走的基础行为。

branches.en: FLOW AND WAVE: counted departures become a measurable flow and then a historical wave.
branches.cn: 流量与浪潮：被计数的离开成为可测量的流量，再成为历史浪潮。

branches.en: LEDGER: emigration is a subtraction in the population account.
branches.cn: 账簿：迁出是人口账户中的一笔减法。

branches.en: ELSEWHERE: the same outflow builds communities abroad and, in finance, moves wealth between tax jurisdictions.
branches.cn: 别处：同一股流出在海外建起社群，在金融中则把财富移出税区。

branches.en: RULES AND NATURE: the state can restrict exits, and in ecology the word names dispersing individuals.
branches.cn: 规则与自然：国家可以限制出境，而在生态学中这个词指扩散的个体。

intro.en: Emigration is a prefix, a root and a suffix, and the family can be read from those pieces.
intro.cn: emigration 由一个前缀、一个词根与一个后缀构成，整个词族都可以按这些成分读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin e- marks motion outward, migrare supplies the root of moving, and -ation turns the verb into the name of the process.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 e- 标记向外移动，migrare 提供「迁移」的词根，-ation 把动词变成过程之名。

items.example: The prefix turns the movement away from home.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把移动转向离开家乡。

items.example: The root carries the idea of changing place.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着更换地点的意思。

items.meaning: to move out of a country
items.exampleCN: 她的家庭在 1901 年迁出。

items.example: The emigrant sold the last of the furniture.
items.exampleCN: 这位迁出者卖掉了最后一件家具。

items.example: It turns the verb into the name of the process.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成过程之名。
向外移民使沿海村庄空了下来。

items.example: It forms the adjective of the process.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示这一过程的形容词。

items.example: The emigratory flow lasted thirty years.
items.exampleCN: 向外移民的流动持续了三十年。

items.example: Migration can be internal or international.
items.exampleCN: 迁移可以是国内的，也可以是跨国的。
